<translate>
<!--T:1-->
Every DragonMineZ command node is registered through Forge's <code>PermissionAPI</code>, so server owners running a permissions mod (LuckPerms, PermissionsEx and the like) can grant fine-grained access instead of relying on blanket operator status. Without a permissions mod, DMZ falls back to vanilla operator levels.
</translate>

<translate>
<!--T:2-->
Nodes are defined in <code>DMZPermissions.java</code>. Each one is registered under the <code>dragonminez</code> namespace, so its full name is <code>dragonminez.&lt;node&gt;</code>, for example <code>dragonminez.admin</code> or <code>dragonminez.dmzstats.set.self</code>. For what each command does, see [[Special:MyLanguage/Commands|Commands]].
</translate>

<translate>
== How a permission check resolves == <!--T:3-->
</translate>
<translate>
<!--T:4-->
For every command gated by a DMZ permission, the check passes if '''any''' of these is true:
</translate>

<translate>
<!--T:5-->
# The player has '''the specific node''' for that action.
# The player has '''<code>dragonminez.admin</code>''', which grants every DMZ permission at once.
# The player is a '''vanilla operator of level 2 or higher''' (<code>player.hasPermissions(2)</code>).
</translate>

<translate>
<!--T:6-->
Commands run from the '''server console or command blocks''' (anything that isn't a player) always pass DMZ permission checks.
</translate>

<syntaxhighlight lang="java">
return PermissionAPI.getPermission(player, node) || PermissionAPI.getPermission(player, ADMIN) || player.hasPermissions(2);
</syntaxhighlight>

<translate>
=== Commands gated by vanilla operator level === <!--T:7-->
</translate>
<translate>
<!--T:8-->
A few commands don't use DMZ nodes at all: they simply require '''operator level 2''', and are not affected by <code>dragonminez.admin</code>.
</translate>

{| class="wikitable"
! <translate><!--T:9--> Command</translate> !! <translate><!--T:10--> Note</translate>
|-
| {{Command|/dmzraid}} || <translate><!--T:11--> Every subcommand (see [[Special:MyLanguage/Raids|Raids]]).</translate>
|-
| {{Command|/dmzworldboss}} || <translate><!--T:12--> Every subcommand '''except <code>results</code>''', which anyone can use (see [[Special:MyLanguage/World Bosses|World Bosses]]).</translate>
|-
| {{Command|/dmztournament}} || <translate><!--T:13--> Every subcommand (see [[Special:MyLanguage/Tournaments|Tournaments]]).</translate>
|-
| {{Command|/dmzquest questnpc}} || <translate><!--T:14--> The quest-NPC spawning subcommands (the rest of <code>/dmzquest</code> uses nodes).</translate>
|}

<translate>
<!--T:15-->
<code>/dmzracial reply accept|reject</code> (answering a Namekian assimilation request) needs no permission at all.
</translate>

<translate>
== Without a permissions mod == <!--T:16-->
</translate>
<translate>
<!--T:17-->
Without LuckPerms, PermissionsEx or a similar mod handling these nodes, each node falls back to its default. In practice, only operators of level 2 or higher can use anything gated by a node that defaults to <code>false</code>. Everyone else only gets the handful of nodes that default to <code>true</code> (see the tables below), which are mostly "view or list your own stuff".
</translate>

<translate>
== Granting nodes with a permissions mod == <!--T:18-->
</translate>
<translate>
<!--T:19-->
Example using LuckPerms syntax (adjust it for the mod you run):
</translate>

<syntaxhighlight lang="text">
/lp user <player> permission set dragonminez.dmzstats.set.self true
/lp group <group> permission set dragonminez.dmzquest.list.others true
/lp user <player> permission set dragonminez.admin true
</syntaxhighlight>

<translate>
<!--T:20-->
DMZ doesn't ship its own grant or revoke command: node management is entirely up to your permissions mod.
</translate>

<translate>
== Node reference == <!--T:21-->
</translate>
<translate>
<!--T:22-->
Nodes default to <code>false</code> (operators and admins only) unless the table says <code>true</code>. Rows written as <code>….self</code> / <code>.others</code> are two nodes: one for using the command on yourself and one for using it on other players.
</translate>

<translate>
=== Admin === <!--T:23-->
</translate>
{| class="wikitable"
! <translate><!--T:24--> Node</translate> !! <translate><!--T:25--> Default</translate> !! <translate><!--T:26--> Grants</translate>
|-
| <code>dragonminez.admin</code> || <code>false</code> || <translate><!--T:27--> Every DMZ permission, at once. Also required (or operator level 2) for <code>/dmzconfig</code>, <code>/dmzrestoreupdate</code> and for using <code>/dmzdebug</code> on another player.</translate>
|}

<translate>
== Applying changes == <!--T:149-->
</translate>
<translate>
<!--T:150-->
Nodes are registered when the mod starts and don't need a config-style reload: grant and revoke changes take effect as soon as your permissions mod applies them (LuckPerms, for instance, applies most changes immediately).
</translate>
